method: Directly opened the original 1961 Kyriale PDF page images 57*, 58*, and 101* and the corresponding original GregoBase source-image witnesses.
Opened all four source GABC downloads: 2522, 1137, 298 and 2412. Reviewed the complete GABC text and structural underlay against what is visibly printed.
Counted note-bearing GABC syllable/melisma tokens using the repository's original source-token parser; these are NOT counts of visually verified printed notes.
No automatic OCR or inferred printed pitches. No claim of complete neume glyph, absolute-pitch, rhythymic mark, episema, accidental or page-by-page underlay parity.

sourceWitnesses.observed: Agnus XVII begins and ends on this page; Kyrie XVIII is printed below it
Sanctus XVIII (including both Hosanna phrases and Benedictus) and the three-invocation ordinary Agnus XVIII
The Requiem repeats the Sanctus XVIII musical family, but has a text-distinct Agnus with dona eis requiem and final sempiternam

scoreSurveys.title: Kyrie XVIII
scoreSurveys.sourceTextAndRepetition: Four notated phrases: Kyrie ×3, Christe ×3, Kyrie ×2, final Kyrie ×1
visuallyObserved: Original print on 57* has four distinct phrase spans with iij., iij., ij. and the unrepeated final variant
The last Kyrie is not the same literal notated source phrase as the first; do not replace it by an automatic repeat
Roman number XVIII begins after the preceding XVII Agnus on the same physical page

scoreSurveys.title: Agnus Dei XVII
scoreSurveys.sourceTextAndRepetition: Three 18-group source underlay invocations; two misericordia endings and final dona nobis pacem
visuallyObserved: Agnus XVII appears above Kyrie XVIII at original printed p.57*, with all three invocations
Printed first two invocations end miserere nobis; the third ends dona nobis pacem
The first two GABC phrase openings differ; do not deduplicate them merely because the Latin ending is repeated

scoreSurveys.title: Sanctus XVIII, including Benedictus
scoreSurveys.sourceTextAndRepetition: Sanctus ×3; Pleni sunt caeli; first Hosanna; Benedictus qui venit; second Hosanna
visuallyObserved: All Sanctus and Benedictus words appear on printed p.58*, and the Sanctus appears again on the Requiem p.101*
The first and second Hosanna are distinct melodic passages in the source transcription; the printed final Hosanna also visibly differs in contour from the initial one
Never split this canonical Sanctus–Benedictus score into two Mass cards merely because a choir might pause between them

scoreSurveys.title: Agnus Dei XVIII (ordinary, not Requiem)
scoreSurveys.sourceTextAndRepetition: Three 18-group source underlay invocations; two miserere nobis and one dona nobis pacem
visuallyObserved: Printed p.58* contains the complete threefold ordinary Agnus XVIII with two miserere nobis endings and the final dona nobis pacem
Printed Requiem p.101* instead uses dona eis requiem twice and an expanded third formula with sempiternam
The current GREGOBASE-2412 GABC is the ordinary form, not the alternate Requiem underlay. It cannot accompany Requiem Agnus text.

nextRequiredPerScore: At enlarged source resolution, map each printed notehead's absolute staff pitch using the original printed clef and compare the encoded GABC pitch, without rewriting the source automatically.
Compare every neume shape, mora, episema, interval, accidental, custodian/bar division, repeat direction and syllable underlay against the exact printed system.
Adjudicate disagreements in an independent discrepancy ledger with image page/system/pitch references, then obtain editorial approval for each score separately.
Do not infer a Requiem GABC from the non-Requiem Agnus XVIII; a separate printed 101* source transcription is required for its extra words and terminal formula.
